title: Charges Laid - Saskatchewan RCMP / Corman Park Police Service Assist - Evade Police
content:

title: UPDATE: Charges Laid - Motor Vehicle Collision - Traffic Restrictions - 22nd Street East And 1st Avenue
content:

The suspect vehicle drove through a red traffic light where it struck another vehicle in the area of 22nd Street and 1st Avenue.

The driver of the stolen vehicle began to flee on foot but was located by officers shortly after. A Conducted Energy Weapon (CEW) was discharged and the man was arrested without further incident.
The 27-year-old female owner of the vehicle who attempted to remove the driver from the stolen vehicle was arrested at the scene of the collision and charged with Obstruction.
The 27-year-old man has been charged with Theft of a Motor Vehicle, Evading Police, Assaulting a Peace Officer, Impaired Driving and Breaching Court-Imposed Conditions.
Both the man and woman involved in this incident are believed to be known to one another.

title: Nearly 200 Arrested Following High-Visibility Enforcement & Crime Disruption Project
content:
For ten days between May 19th and 30th, the Saskatoon Police Service conducted a high visibility enforcement and crime disruption project within areas of increased criminal activity as part of a proactive approach to a city-wide safety plan. The project, organized by the Criminal Investigations Bureau with the support of the Patrol Bureau and Operational Support Bureau, redeployed resources from the Crime Reduction Team, Break and Enter Comprehensive Action Program, Guns and Gangs Unit, Warrant Enforcement Unit, Tactical Support Unit, Alternative Response Unit, and Serious Violent Offender Response Program in a highly visible capacity to respond to in-progress violent crime and conduct priority violent offender management.
As a result of this project, a total of 578 project-initiated calls for service were generated and 256 patrol-level responses were made leading to 196 new arrests and 181 new charges laid on 98 persons. Through this proactive initiative, 292 outstanding warrants were also executed on 117 offenders. In addition to these arrests, police seized; one real and three imitation firearms, 23 bladed weapons, six canisters of bear spray, five blunt weapons, and the following quantities of drugs:
20.37 grams of methamphetamine
16.65 grams of cocaine
7.38 grams of fentanyl
17 gabapentin pills
2 pregabalin pills
1 unknown pill
“This project demonstrates that strategic investment in the right resources being deployed with purpose and supported by partnership can suppress crime in our community while removing violent offenders and dangerous weapons from our streets.”, says Chief Cameron McBride, “Pairing community partnerships with focused enforcement is a key component to keeping Saskatoon safe.”
Through a whole-of-city approach to safety, the Saskatoon Police Service remains committed to working collaboratively with public safety and community partners to proactively address crime in our community while prioritizing investigations into outstanding warrants that involve prolific violent offenders. Community members are encouraged to continue reporting crime and suspicious activity in their neighbourhoods to police by calling 306-975-8300 or, in an emergency, 9-1-1. Every report made matters; assisting in analyzing crime and informing police of what resources are needed and where.

title: Charges Laid - Theft / Evade Police - 1700 Block Of Preston Avenue North
content:
Two women were arrested over the weekend following a reported theft that led to an evade police incident.
On August 1, 2026 at around 9:30 a.m., police were dispatched to the 1700 block of Preston Avenue North for a report of a woman who had stolen from a business. Call information stated the woman was in a vehicle in the parking lot.
Upon police arrival, officers located the vehicle as it was beginning to leave. Officers activated their emergency lights to initiate a traffic stop, however, the driver did not stop. The suspect vehicle then hit a vehicle before fleeing at a high rate of speed southbound on Preston Avenue. Shortly after, officers disengaged before locating the suspect vehicle unoccupied and left running. Police located and arrested two suspects shortly after. It was also learned that the vehicle had been reported as stolen.
As a result, a 30-year-old woman and a 38-year-old woman have been charged with Possession of Property Obtained by Crime Over $5000 and Theft. The 30-year-old has also been charged with Dangerous Driving, Evading Police and Failure to Stop at the Scene of a Collision.

title: Additional Info: Update: Mischief Incident - Faith-Based Organization - 700 Block McKinnon Ave S
content:
Court Info # 991348284
Release 2026-0506
August 14, 2026 12:18 PM
One man has been identified and charged following an investigation into eggs being thrown at a building and vehicles associated to a faith-based organization.
Through investigation and with public assistance, the suspect was identified as a 31-year-old man from Dundurn, SK. Following his identification, arrangements were made for him to turn himself in to the Saskatoon Police Service Headquarters on August 13, 2026 where he was charged with three counts of Mischief Under $5,000 and later released on conditions.
“As a police service, we recognize the significance of incidents that target faith-based communities and the impact on their sense of safety and belonging. Upon receiving the police report, the Community Engagement Division and the SPS Hate Crimes Unit were engaged, and with assistance from the community, the suspect was identified, arrested, and charged with Mischief,” says Superintendent James Oliver. “In Canada, ‘hate crime’ is generally used as an umbrella term, not a specific charge under the Criminal Code. Any evidence that an offence was motivated by bias, prejudice, or hate is considered by the court as an aggravating factor during sentencing.”
